title: Total Rewards + Career Flex Guide: Allocations, Leave, and Tools
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This guide summarizes Redwood’s integrated approach to total rewards, career ladders, and the internal tools that make benefit allocations and role mobility operational. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, new hires, and engineers planning rotations. The goal is to reduce surprises, speed approvals, and align people decisions with product and business priorities.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time Redwood employees and long-term contractors (≥ 6 months).
- Covers compensation-adjacent benefits (cash, equity refresh policy summary), time-off programs, learning and wellness budgets, role mobility mechanisms, and the tool workflows to request/approve changes.

Summary of Key Principles:
- Predictable baseline: core benefits are standardized by level band to support mobility and fairness.
- Flexible top-ups: team-level discretion exists for role-based allowances and one-off flex credits.
- Career-enabled benefits: learning and rotation mechanisms are designed to shorten time-to-impact for lateral and upward moves.

1) Career Ladders and Role Framework (high level)

Overview of career streams:
- Individual Contributor (IC): IC1 → IC2 → IC3 → Senior IC → Staff → Principal
- Manager track: Mgr1 (first-time manager) → Mgr2 → Senior Manager → Director
- Engineering leadership and cross-functional leader ladders mirror scope but have different expectations around org impact.

Competency expectations (one-sentence summaries per band):
- IC1: Delivers small-scope features; follows existing patterns; requires mentorship.
- IC2: Owns medium-sized components; contributes to design; influences peers.
- IC3: Owns service-level outcomes; mentors others; leads moderate designs.
- Senior IC / Staff: Shapes architecture; drives cross-team initiatives; recognized as go-to domain expert.

Promotion cadence and signals:
- Typical eligibility: 12–24 months at level with demonstrated increasing scope and impact.
- Required artifacts for promotion packet: updated resume, 3 peer reviews, manager recommendation, 2 example deliverables, and a short impact memo (≤ 2 pages).
- Review process SLA: People-ops acknowledges packet within 3 business days and target decision within 30 days for standard promotions.

2) Total Rewards: Elements and Typical Allocations

Base compensation and equity:
- Base pay is banded by level and geography. Managers consult compensation band table (HR system). Equity awards follow the annual refresh cadence; exceptions require People-ops approval.

Variable and discretionary pools:
- Performance bonus: annual, paid in Q1 based on company and individual results.
- Spot awards: up to $2k manager-level approval; $10k+ requires director-level signoff and People-ops.

Flexible benefit credits (new 2025 program):
- Every employee receives a flexible credit pool of $2,000/year to allocate across three categories: Learning, Wellbeing, and Home Office. Unused credits do not roll over.
- Example allocations: Learning (up to $1,200), Wellbeing (up to $800), Home Office (up to $500) — teams can combine credits up to the yearly cap.

Parental and care leave highlights:
- Primary parental leave: up to 16 weeks fully paid for birth parents.
- Secondary leave: up to 8 weeks fully paid for non-birthing parents and partners.
- Caregiver leave: up to 4 weeks paid for critical family illness.
- Continuation of benefits during leave; manager check-ins required at 30/90 days.

Sabbatical and long-tenure perks:
- Long-tenure sabbatical: 6 weeks paid sabbatical at five-year anniversaries (eligible after 5 consecutive years).
- Innovation sabbaticals: up to 2 weeks to pursue open-source/community projects with manager approval.

3) Learning & Mobility Programs

Learning fund and career credits:
- Learning credit (part of flexible pool): default $1,200/year. Pre-approval needed for programs > $500.
- Transferable learning: up to $600 of unused learning credit may be repurposed once per year toward certification/test fees.

Role swap and rotation windows:
- 90-day rotations (internal temp assignments) are supported for skills development. Managers must approve and confirm primary deliverables before rotation start.
- Rotation approval checklist: capacity sign-off, 1-page learning plan, and a temporary owner for in-flight work.

Fast-track lateral moves (pilot program):
- For high-priority technical roles, a ‘fast-track’ mobility path reduces notice-to-offer timelines to 2 weeks with hiring manager and people-ops alignment.

4) Onboarding and Hiring: Process Map and First 90 Days

Pre-boarding (day -14 to day 0):
- Hiring manager checklist: confirm laptop/ergonomics order, assign buddy, plan first-week meetings, submit access request to IT (SSO groups).
- People-ops tasks: create HR profile, add to payroll, schedule benefits orientation, enroll in flexible credit program.

Day 0–7: foundational ramp
- Goals: account access, meet immediate team, complete security & compliance training, first pairing session.
- Must-complete items: SSO login, security training, org chart read, assigned buddy check-in.

Day 30: impact milestone
- Deliverable: first small ticket/bug fix or doc contribution. Manager 1:1 to review clarity, blockers, and learning goals.

Day 60: cross-team exposure
- Recommended: 1 tech design discussion outside immediate team; update learning plan; apply for learning credits if needed.

Day 90: calibrate and plan
- Outcomes: performance calibration conversation; if applicable, start career-path discussion and identify potential rotations.

Onboarding tooling and SLAs:
- Primary tools: Okta (SSO), Lever (recruiting), Rippling (HR/payroll), Confluence (docs), Jira (work), Slack (comms), 1Password (secrets).
- Access SLA: IT aims to grant core accesses by Day 1 and full role access by Day 7. Escalation contact: it-access@redwood.com.

5) Internal Tools and Request Workflows (step-by-step)

Requesting flexible credits or one-off allowances:
1. Employee files request via Confluence form (link in footer) including justification and cost estimate.
2. Manager reviews and approves in-line, then forwards to People-ops for policy check.
3. People-ops issues funds or approves purchase within 5 business days.

Requesting role change or rotation:
1. Employee communicates interest to manager and opens a "Mobility Request" Jira ticket (template tag: MOBILITY-REQ).
2. Manager and receiving manager coordinate capacity; People-ops validates compensation/equity implications.
3. Formal offer and start date issued; target timeline: 2–6 weeks depending on complexity.

Emergency access or expedited hires:
- For production-critical hiring or access needs, the oncall IT lead can approve temporary access for up to 72 hours. Post-event retrospective required.

6) Approvals, Ownership, and SLAs

Owner matrix (who does what):
- People-ops: policy design, promotion process ownership, flexible credit disbursement, and final escalation.
- Hiring manager: day-to-day onboarding, learning plan approval, promotion packet initiation.
- IT/Security: access provisioning, device enrollment, and secrets management.
- Finance: payroll, equity grant processing, and expense reconciliation.

Service level targets:
- Onboarding access SLA: core access Day 1 / full role access Day 7.
- Promotion decision SLA: acknowledge 3 business days / decision target 30 calendar days.
- Flexible credit request: People-ops response within 5 business days.

7) Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I roll over unused flexible credits?
A: No. Credits reset on Jan 1 each year and do not roll over, with one exception for transferable learning noted above.

Q: Who approves cross-functional rotations?
A: Both the origin and receiving manager plus People-ops must sign off. Use the rotation checklist in the Mobility Jira template.

Q: I need a faster hire for a production incident. What is the path?
A: Mark the job as "Priority: Critical" in Lever and copy it to the internal hire channel. IT oncall can approve 72-hour access. Submit a retro within 10 business days.

8) Change Log and Governance

- 2024-09-15: Initial draft and launch of flexible credit pilot.
- 2025-03-01: Added transferable learning rule and adjusted parental leave wording.
- 2026-02-14: Updated SLAs for promotion decisions and clarified rotation checklist.
